pages.d: Download and install Kadr on Windows, get past the SmartScreen warning, let Kadr set up FFmpeg and create your first project.

s.x: From download to your first project in about five minutes. Kadr is free, needs no account and works offline.

Kadr is published on its GitHub Releases page. Open the newest release and, under Assets, download the installer: FileWhat it is Kadr-Setup-X.Y.Z-x64.exeThe installer — choose this one. It installs Kadr for your user account (no administrator rights needed), adds a Start menu entry and keeps Kadr up to date. Kadr-X.Y.Z-windows-x64-portable.zipThe portable version: unzip and run, nothing is installed. See Portable mod
Double-click Kadr-Setup-…-x64.exe in your Downloads folder.
Kadr is not code-signed yet, so Windows may show a blue window saying “Windows protected your PC”. Click More info, then Run anyway. This warning appears for most new apps from small publishers.

The installer speaks English and Ukrainian. Accept the licence; Kadr installs into your user folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Kadr). Two options are ticked by default: Create a desktop shortcut, and Add kadrctl and kadr-mcp to PATH — the second one is only needed if you plan to connect an AI assistant, but leaving it on does no harm.
The editor window uses Microsoft Edge WebView2, which is already part of Windows 11 and most Windows 10 PCs. If it is missing, the installer points you to Microsoft's free download.

Leave Launch Kadr ticked on the last page, or start Kadr from the Start menu later. Want to be extra sure the file is genuine? In PowerShell run Get-FileHash .\Kadr-Setup-X.Y.Z-x64.exe and compare the result with the matching line in SHA256SUMS.txt.

Kadr reads and writes video with FFmpeg, a free program that is not bundled with Kadr. The first time you start Kadr, it checks for FFmpeg. If it can't find one, the Set up FFmpeg window appears: The first-run FFmpeg window. In the desktop app there is also a button “I have FFmpeg — choose folder”. Download now (recommended) — Kadr downloads FFmpeg 7.1 for Windows (about 100 MB), checks that the file is intact and ke
The home screen lists your projects. Start a new one with Create project.

Click Create project (or press Ctrl+N) for a normal 16:9 video. For TikTok, Reels or Shorts click Vertical 9:16; for an Instagram post, Square 1:1. The editor opens right away. You can change the shape later — see Projects.
In the Media tab click Import (Ctrl+I) or drag files from File Explorer onto the window. More in Import media.
Click the + on a media card, or drag the card down onto the timeline. Clips on the main track line up one after another automatically.

Move the playhead (the white line) to a spot and press Ctrl+B to cut, select the unwanted part and press Delete. Add a title from the Text tab and music from Media. The Timeline editing page has all the details.

Click Export in the top-right corner (Ctrl+E), keep the suggested settings and click Export. Your video lands in Videos\Kadr. See Export. Kadr saves every change immediately — there is no Save button. Made a mistake? Ctrl+Z undoes it.

Almost everything works straight after installation. Two smart features use free AI models that run on your own computer and need a one-time setup with Python: Automatic captions and transcript editing — needs Python and faster-whisper. See Captions → What you need. Background removal — needs Python and rembg. See AI tools.

MinimumRecommended WindowsWindows 10 (version 1809), 64-bitWindows 11, 64-bit ProcessorAny 64-bit processor6 cores or more Memory4 GB8 GB, or 16 GB for 4K video GraphicsNot requiredAn NVIDIA, Intel or AMD graphics card makes export faster DiskAbout 1 GB for Kadr and FFmpeg, plus room for your projectsAn SSD InternetOnly for the one-time FFmpeg download and update checks. Editing works offline.

Menu and Back to home. Menu holds New project, Import media, Undo and Redo (with the name of the step, e.g. “Undo Split”), Keyboard shortcuts, API documentation, Settings and Check for updates. A small dot on Menu means an update is ready. The arrow ← takes you back to the home screen. Project name. Click it to rename the project, then press Enter. Shortcuts and Export. Shortcuts lists every keyboard shortcut (Ctrl+/

Everything you can add to a video lives here, sorted into tabs. Pick a tab at the top, a category on the left, and click a card to preview it. Click + on a card (or double-click it) to add it at the playhead, or drag it onto the timeline. Shows your video exactly as it will be exported. Press Space to play and pause. You can click a clip in the picture to select it and then move, scale or rotate it with the mouse. Below the picture are the time, the play button, the preview quality, the Ratio menu and full screen. More in Player & preview.

The settings of whatever is selected. Select a video clip and you get the tabs Video, Audio, Speed, Animation and Adjustment; select a title and you get Text and Animation; an audio clip shows Basic, Voice changer and Speed. When nothing is selected, the inspector shows the Draft settings of the project: frame rate and canvas background. Every change is saved and can be undone with Ctrl+Z. Many sliders have a small d

The row above the timeline. From left to right: Select / Split tool (A / B), Undo, Redo; Split, Delete left, Delete right, Delete; Add marker, Freeze frame, Reverse, Mirror, Rotate, Crop; Smart tools — scene split, silence removal, auto reframe, separate audio and auto captions; on the right: Main track magnet, Auto snapping, Linkage, Preview axis, timeline zoom, Zoom to fit and Hide timeline. Hover over any button t

Each track row starts with small buttons: a padlock to lock the track (protect it from edits), an eye to hide it and a speaker to mute it. The main video track also has a Cover button for choosing the project's thumbnail.

Your video laid out in time, from left to right. The ruler at the top shows the time; click or drag on it to move the playhead (the white vertical line). Tracks are stacked: the lowest video track is the main track, picture-in-picture clips, stickers, text, effects and filters go on tracks above it, and audio goes below. Coloured flags on the ruler are markers. Everything about editing here is in Timeline editing.

Drag the thin borders between the panels to make the library, inspector or timeline bigger. Press Ctrl+. to hide the timeline and get a large player; press it again to bring it back. Edited by someone else? If an AI assistant or a script changes your project, the editor updates live and shows a short message such as “Edited via MCP”. Those changes can be undone like your own. See the AI documentation.

pages.d: Create, open, rename, duplicate and delete projects on the Kadr home screen, and set the video shape (ratio), frame rate, background and cover.

s.x: A project is one video you are working on. Kadr keeps all your projects on the home screen and saves every change the moment you make it.

Kadr opens on the home screen. To get back to it from the editor, click the ← arrow in the top bar or choose Menu → Back to home. Your projects, newest first. Each card shows the length and the shape of the video. Create project — a new 16:9 video (1920×1080, 30 frames per second). Shortcut: Ctrl+N, which also works inside the editor. Vertical 9:16 — for TikTok, Reels and Shorts (1080×1920). Square 1:1 — for square p

Click a project's picture (or double-click the card) to open it. For everything else, click the … button under the card: Open Rename — type the new name and press Enter. Duplicate — makes an independent copy, handy for trying out a different version. Delete — asks for confirmation first. The … menu of a project card. Deleting a project cannot be undone. Kadr removes the project itself, but your original video, photo

You can change the shape of your video at any time with the Ratio button below the player. Kadr offers 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:3, 3:4, 21:9, 2.35:1, 2:1, 1.85:1 and 5.8-inch (a tall phone screen). The Ratio menu, and the Draft settings shown when no clip is selected. When the shape changes, every clip is fitted into the new frame and any empty area is filled with the canvas background (see below). Titles and stickers keep

Click an empty part of the timeline so that nothing is selected. The inspector on the right then shows Draft settings: Frame rate — 24, 25, 30, 50 or 60 fps. 30 fps suits most social videos; use 25 fps if your camera records PAL video, 60 fps for smooth gaming or sports footage. Canvas background — what shows where no clip covers the frame: a Color (pick one of the swatches) or a Blur — a blurred, enlarged copy of th

The cover is the frame used as the project's thumbnail. Click Cover at the start of the main track, drag the slider or pick one of the frames, then click Save. Use playhead takes the frame under the playhead; Reset goes back to the first frame. Choosing the cover frame.

There is no Save button: Kadr saves after every single change, and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo. Projects are stored in your Windows profile, in %APPDATA%\Kadr\projects (one folder per project). A project contains only links to your media files, not copies — so keep your original files where they are. If you do move them, Kadr shows them as missing and lets you relink them. s.x: Before you can edit, bring your videos, photos and music into the project. They appear in the Media tab, ready to be placed on the timeline. The Media tab. Right-click a card for more options.

Import button. Open the Media tab and click Import. A normal Windows file window opens; select one or several files (hold Ctrl or Shift to pick many) and click Open. Keyboard. Press Ctrl+I anywhere in the editor. The same is in Menu → Import media. Drag and drop. Drag files — or a whole folder — from File Explorer onto the Kadr window. When you drop a folder, every video, audio and photo file inside it is imported. A

The chips All, Videos, Photos and Audio filter the list; the number on the right is how many items are shown. Search media finds files by name. A green Added label means the file is already used on the timeline. The time in the corner is the length of the clip; a small icon marks photos and audio.

Hover a card and click +, or select it and press Enter. Videos and photos are added to the end of the main track; audio goes onto an audio track, starting at the playhead. Or drag the card onto the timeline exactly where you want it. Dropped on the main track, the clip is inserted at the nearest cut and the clips after it move right. 4K, HEVC and other heavy videos can make the preview stutter. A proxy is a small, easy-to-play copy (540p) that Kadr uses only while you edit. Right-click the video card and choose Create proxy; a percentage on the card shows the progress, and the menu then says Proxy created. The player and the timeline use the proxy automatically. Export always uses the original file, so the final video keeps its full quality. Prox

If you move, rename or delete an original file, its card is marked as missing and its clips can't be shown. Right-click the card, choose Link media… and type the new full path of the file (for example D:\Footage\beach.mp4). Everything on the timeline comes back as it was.

The Library entry on the left of the Media tab is reserved for built-in stock footage, which is not available yet. For ready-made backgrounds, countdowns and colour bars, use the generated media in the Stickers tab. For music, import your own audio files.

pages.d: Select, move, trim, split and delete clips on the Kadr timeline; use the magnet, snapping, tracks, markers, copy and paste, speed and undo.

s.x: The timeline is where your video takes shape. This page covers everything you do there, from the first cut to markers and speed changes. Toolbar and timeline. The selected clip has a white outline; the white line is the playhead.

Main track — the lowest video track, with the Cover button at its start. Your story goes here. Clips on it always sit next to each other without gaps (see magnet). Tracks above the main track — overlays (picture-in-picture), stickers, text and captions, effects, filters and adjustment layers. What is higher covers what is lower. Audio tracks — below the main track: music, voice-overs and sound effects. Tracks are cre

Playhead. Click the ruler or drag along it to move the playhead; the player shows that moment. Space plays and pauses, ← / → step one frame. Zoom. Hold Ctrl and turn the mouse wheel over the timeline, press Ctrl+= / Ctrl+-, or use the zoom slider on the right of the toolbar. Zoom to fit (the arrows button next to it) shows the whole video. Scroll. The mouse wheel scrolls up and down when there are many tracks; Shift+

Click a clip to select it. Its settings appear in the inspector on the right. Shift+click or Ctrl+click adds clips to the selection (or removes them). Drag a rectangle starting on an empty part of the timeline to select every clip it touches. Hold Shift or Ctrl to add to the current selection. Ctrl+A selects all clips on unlocked tracks. Click an empty spot to deselect everything (this also moves the playhead there).

Move: drag a clip left or right, or up and down to another track of the same kind. A video can move between the main track and overlay tracks; if the spot is taken, Kadr makes a new track for it. Trim: point at the left or right edge of a clip — the cursor turns into a double arrow — and drag to shorten or lengthen it. A video can't get longer than its original recording. While you drag, a guide line shows where the

At the playhead: move the playhead to where you want the cut and press Ctrl+B or click Split in the toolbar. If a clip is selected and under the playhead, that clip is cut; otherwise the main-track clip under the playhead is. With the Split tool: press B (or pick Split in the tool menu at the left of the toolbar). The pointer becomes a cross — click anywhere on a clip to cut it there. Press A to go back to the Select

Delete (or Backspace) removes the selected clips. On the main track the following clips slide left to close the gap. Q — Delete left: removes the part of the clip before the playhead. W — Delete right: removes the part after the playhead. The fastest way to tidy a talking video: play it, stop where a mistake starts, press Q… or select a stretch and press Delete. Even faster: let Kadr cut pauses and filler words for y
Ctrl+C copies the selected clips, Ctrl+X cuts them, Ctrl+V pastes at the playhead. Ctrl+D duplicates the selected clip right after itself.

Right-click on…You get A clipCopy, Cut, Paste, Split, Duplicate, Freeze frame and Extract audio (video clips), the Smart tools that fit the clip, Delete An empty spotPaste, Add marker here A marker on the rulerDelete marker A transition badgeSelect transition, Apply to all, Remove transition

s.t: More clip tools in the toolbar
s.x: ButtonWhat it does Freeze frameInserts a 3-second still of the frame under the playhead into the video clip. ReversePlays the selected video backwards. Click again to play it forwards. MirrorFlips the picture left to right. Click again to flip it back. RotateTurns the picture 90° clockwise. CropOpens the crop window: drag the frame, pick Free, 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:3 or 3:4, then Confirm.

Select a video or audio clip and open the Speed tab in the inspector. Normal — a single speed from 0.1× (slow motion) to 100× (time-lapse). You can also type the new Duration and Kadr works out the speed. Keep pitch stops voices from sounding like chipmunks when sped up. Curve — speed that changes over the clip: Montage, Hero, Bullet, Jump cut, Flash in, Flash out, or draw your own. On the main track, the following c

Four switches on the right side of the toolbar change how the timeline behaves. Each is highlighted when it is on. SwitchWhen on Main track magnet (N)Clips on the main track always stick together: deleting or shortening a clip closes the gap, inserting one pushes the rest right. Turn it off to leave gaps on purpose. Auto snappingWhile you drag, clip edges jump to other clip edges, the playhead, markers and the start

The buttons at the start of each track row: Padlock — locks the track. Its clips can't be selected, moved or changed until you unlock it. Handy for protecting finished music or captions. Eye — hides the track in the player and in the export, without deleting anything. Speaker — mutes the sound of the whole track.

Markers are little flags on the ruler that help you remember important moments, such as beats of the music or places to cut. Press M or click Add marker in the toolbar to drop a marker at the playhead. Right-clicking an empty spot gives Add marker here. Drag a marker along the ruler to move it. Clips snap to markers. Right-click a marker and choose Delete marker to remove it. Markers can also have a name and a colour

Ctrl+Z undoes the last change, Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes it. The arrow buttons at the left of the toolbar do the same, and their tooltips — like the items in Menu — tell you which step you are about to undo (“Undo Split”). Every change is one step, including changes made by an AI assistant.

Press Ctrl+. or click the last button on the right of the toolbar to fold the timeline away; do it again to bring it back. You can also drag the border above the toolbar to give the timeline more or less height.

pages.d: Play your video, move, scale and rotate clips right in the picture, zoom and pan the canvas, show safe zones, use masks and blend modes, and pick the preview quality.

s.x: The player shows your video exactly as it will be exported. It is also an editing surface: you can grab titles, stickers and overlays right in the picture and put them where you want. A selected title with its handles, and the safe zones of a vertical video.

Press Space or the round play button to play and pause. ← and → move one frame back or forward — perfect for finding the exact spot for a cut. The time on the left reads hours:minutes:seconds:frames, followed by the total length. The square button at the bottom right shows the player full screen; Esc leaves it.

The button next to Ratio (it shows Full, 1/2 or 1/4) and the … menu at the top right set how sharp the preview is: Full quality — sharpest. Half — faster. Quarter — fastest, for slower computers or very heavy projects. This only affects the preview. Exports always use full quality. Kadr remembers your choice. If the preview still stutters, create proxies for your largest videos.

Make sure the Move tool (the arrow at the top of the player, V) is active and playback is paused. To…Do this Select a clipClick it in the picture. A frame with handles appears. If several clips are stacked on top of each other, Alt+click picks the next one underneath. Shift+click or Ctrl+click adds to the selection. MoveDrag the clip. It snaps to the centre lines, the edges of the frame and other elements, and guide

The zoom button at the top of the player (it says Fit or a percentage) offers Zoom to fit (Shift+F), 50% (Shift+0), 100% (Shift+1) and 200% (Shift+2). Shift+= and Shift+- zoom in and out step by step; Ctrl or Shift + mouse wheel zooms around the pointer. To look around a zoomed canvas, pick the Hand tool (H) and drag, drag with the middle mouse button, or just turn the mouse wheel. Press V to return to the Move tool.

Social apps cover parts of your video with their own buttons and captions. Click the dashed-square button at the top of the player to show guides: Vertical videos get a Top bar area, a Caption & controls area at the bottom, a Buttons column on the right and the Safe for text area in between. Keep titles and captions inside it. Other shapes get the classic Action safe and Title safe frames. The guides are only shown i

A video or photo placed above the main track is an overlay (picture-in-picture). Select it and use the inspector: Video → Basic → Blend — Opacity and 14 blend modes (Darken, Screen, Overlay, Multiply, Lighten, Hard light, Soft light, Linear burn, Color burn, Color dodge, Add, Difference, Exclusion). Video → Mask — hide part of the clip with a Linear, Mirror, Circle, Rectangle, Heart or Star shape. Sliders set the pos

pages.d: Add titles and text in Kadr: templates, fonts and colours, outlines, shadows and glow, word-art effects, curved text and letter-by-letter animations.

s.x: Titles, lower thirds, labels and call-outs are all text clips. Start from a template or plain text, then style and animate it in the inspector. Text templates on the left, the selected title in the player, its settings on the right.
New text starts at the playhead, so first put the playhead where the text should appear.

Open the Text tab. Under Templates, the Default category has plain white text; the other categories — Trending, Basic, Title, Caption, Fancy, Social, Lower third, Neon and Animated — have ready-made looks. Click a card to see its name and description.
Click + on the card or double-click it, or drag it onto the timeline. A text clip appears on a text track (3 seconds long for plain text) and is selected, ready to edit.

With the text clip selected, the inspector shows the Text tab. Type your words into the large box at the top of Basic; press Enter for a new line. The change is applied when you click elsewhere. To change the length of the text on screen, drag the edges of its clip on the timeline. To place it, drag it in the player.

The Font section of Text → Basic contains: Font — Kadr's built-in fonts plus every font installed on your computer. Cyrillic and other alphabets fall back to a matching system font automatically. Size, Bold, Italic, Underline and left / centre / right alignment. Case — Aa (as typed), AB (capitals), ab (lower case), Ab Cd (title case). Your original words are kept, so you can switch back. Color — a swatch or the colou

Below the font settings are sections you switch on with their toggle. Each has its own colour and sliders: SectionWhat it adds StrokeAn outline around the letters — makes text readable on busy footage. Extra outlineSecond and further outlines for a sticker-like look. BackgroundA box behind the text, with opacity and rounded corners. ShadowA drop shadow with opacity, blur, distance and angle. GlowA soft light around t

Text effects are complete looks — gradients, metal, glow, 3D, outlines, retro — in one click. For new text: in the Text tab, switch from Templates to Text effects and add a card. You get text in that style. For existing text: select it and open Text → Effects in the inspector. Pick a card, or None to remove the effect. An effect simply fills in the Basic settings (gradient, glow, outlines, 3D), so you can fine-tune i

Text → Animate. Open Text → Animate. Animations here move the letters and words inside the text: In — how the text appears: Typewriter, Letter rise, Letter drop, Karaoke sweep, Random spell, Word pop and more. Out — how it disappears. Loop — a movement that repeats while the text is visible, such as a wave or a pulse. Click a card to apply it, then set its Duration (or Period for loops) below the grid. None removes i

Text → Transform — exact position, scale, rotation and blending of the text. Text → Speech — reads the text aloud with a computer voice and places the speech under it. See Text to speech. Save to My kit — the bookmark button next to the sub-tabs saves the style so you can apply it to other texts in any project. See My kit. For subtitles that follow speech, use Captions instead of typing them by hand. Keep important t

pages.d: Create subtitles automatically with offline Whisper speech recognition, style them with word highlighting, edit cues, import and export SRT files, and cut your video by editing its transcript.

s.x: Kadr can listen to your video and write the subtitles for you — on your own computer, without uploading anything. You can then restyle them, fix words, save them as an SRT file, or even edit the video by deleting words from its transcript.
Speech recognition uses Whisper (through the free faster-whisper package), which runs on Python. You set it up once:
Download Python 3.9 or newer from python.org and run the installer. On its first page tick Add python.exe to PATH.
Open PowerShell (Start menu → type “PowerShell”) and run:
Still in PowerShell, run the line below. It downloads the recommended small model (about 500 MB). This is the only step that needs the internet.

Open Captions → Auto captions. If it still says Speech recognition is not set up, click Check again (or restart Kadr). When it works, the panel says it runs offline with Whisper on your CPU or NVIDIA graphics card. An NVIDIA graphics card makes recognition several times faster. Without one, choose the small or base model. If Kadr picks the wrong Python, see Troubleshooting.

Captions → Auto captions. Open the Captions tab; Auto captions is selected on the left. Language used in video — keep Detect automatically, or choose the language (about 100 are available, including English and Ukrainian). Choosing it is a little more accurate. Model — tiny is fastest, small is the balanced default, medium and large-v3 are the most accurate but slow without a graphics card. Models you haven't downloa

Captions → Edit captions. The highlighted caption is the one under the playhead. Choose Edit captions on the left. Every caption is listed with its start and end time. Click into the text to correct it: Key / buttonEffect EnterSplits the caption in two at the text cursor. Ctrl+EnterStarts a new line inside the same caption. Backspace at the very startMerges the caption with the previous one. Delete at the very endMer

Choose Styles on the left and click a style to apply it to every caption. The chips filter the 15 styles: Trending, Basic, Word highlight, Social and Boxed. Styles marked word light up each word as it is spoken — the karaoke look popular on TikTok and Reels. They work because auto captions know the timing of every word. To fine-tune the highlight, select a caption on the timeline and open Text → Animate in the inspec

Upload file imports subtitles you already have: type the full path of the file, pick a style, optionally an Offset in seconds (to shift them), tick Replace the current captions if needed, and click Import. Supported: SubRip .srt, WebVTT .vtt, Advanced SubStation .ass/.ssa and lyrics .lrc (word tags in LRC become karaoke timing). Download saves your captions as SubRip (.srt), WebVTT (.vtt), plain text (.txt) or lyrics

s.t: Edit the video by editing text
s.x: The Transcript tab. The word under the playhead is highlighted. The Transcript tab shows everything that is said in your video as text. Deleting words here cuts them out of the video — the easiest way to clean up interviews, vlogs and podcasts. Open the Transcript tab. If clips have no transcript yet, pick the Spoken language and click Transcribe. (Clips that already have auto captions are transcribed.) Click a word

Fillers — removes hesitations such as “um”, “uh”, “er” and, when used as fillers, “like” or “you know”. English, Ukrainian and Russian are recognised. The number on the button tells you how many were found; they are shown with a dotted underline in the text. Remove pauses — shortens every silence longer than the number you set (in seconds) down to 0.3 s. Pauses are shown as small grey badges between words. Captions —

pages.d: Add transitions between clips, video effects and filters, grade colour with basic sliders, HSL and curves, animate anything with keyframes and save your favourite looks to My kit.

s.x: Transitions smooth out cuts, effects add movement and atmosphere, filters and colour tools set the mood. Everything in this page is original to Kadr and rendered on your computer.

The Transitions tab and the Transition panel of a selected transition. A transition plays between two clips that touch each other on the same track (usually the main track). There are 68 of them, from simple fades and slides to 3D cubes, iris shapes, light leaks and glitches.

On the timeline, click the left clip of the two clips you want to join. Open the Transitions tab. The hint at the top confirms “Applies to the cut after the selected clip”. Click + on a transition (or double-click it). You can also simply drag a transition onto the cut on the timeline. The transition appears as a small badge on the cut. Apply to all (next to the hint) puts the highlighted transition on every cut of t

Click the badge on the timeline to open the Transition panel in the inspector (or select the left clip and click the transition's name under Video → Transition to next clip). There you can set the Duration, the Direction and Softness where a transition supports them, swap it for another under Replace, Apply to all, or Remove it. With the badge selected, Delete removes it too. A transition can be at most half as long

An effect layer selected: its own sliders appear in the inspector. The Effects tab has 56 effects in categories such as Party, Retro, Glitch, Lens, Light, Sparkle, Comics, Nature and Split screen. Use them in two ways: As a layer: click + (or drag the card to the timeline). The effect goes on its own effect track at the playhead and affects everything below it for as long as the effect clip lasts. Drag its edges to c

Filters change the colours of the picture in one click — warm, cool, film, black-and-white, vintage and 70 more, in 18 categories. On one clip: select the clip, click a filter card, then Apply “…” to clip. On a stretch of the video: click + on a card. A filter layer is added at the playhead and colours everything below it. With a filtered clip or a filter layer selected, the panel at the top of the Filters tab shows
Select a video or photo clip and open the Adjustment tab of the inspector. It has three pages: Adjustment → Basic.

Color: Temperature (warmer/cooler), Tint, Saturation, Hue. Lightness: Exposure, Brightness, Contrast, Shine, Highlights, Shadows. Effects: Sharpen, Vignette (dark corners), Fade, Grain. LUT: type the path of a .cube colour-grading file and set its intensity. Auto adjust analyses the frame and fixes exposure, contrast, white balance and saturation in one click. Reset clears all colour settings, including HSL and curve

Change one colour without touching the others. Click one of the eight colour dots (red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, magenta) and move Hue, Saturation and Lightness — for example make the sky deeper blue or the grass less yellow. A small dot marks the bands you have changed. Adjustment → HSL with the blue band adjusted. Adjustment → Curves with the Contrast preset.

For precise control of brightness and colour. pages.d: Add music and sound effects, set volume and fades, change voices, reduce noise, separate audio from video and create voice-overs with text to speech — including ElevenLabs voices.

s.x: Good sound makes a video. Kadr lets you add music and sound effects, balance volumes, clean up voices and even create a voice-over from text. Sound effects on the left; the settings of the selected audio clip on the right.

Kadr has no built-in music library — bring your own tracks. Import MP3, WAV, M4A, FLAC or other audio files in the Media tab, then click + on the card or drag it onto the timeline. Audio goes on its own track below the video and can be moved, trimmed and split like any clip. Only use music you have the right to use. Platforms such as YouTube may mute or block videos with copyrighted songs.

Select an audio clip — or a video clip and its Audio tab — to see Basic: Volume in decibels (dB): 0 dB is the original level, −6 dB is about half as loud, all the way down to −∞ (silent); up to +20 dB to boost quiet recordings. The diamond next to it lets you animate the volume, for example to lower the music while someone speaks. Fade in / Fade out — the sound rises at the start and dies away at the end, in seconds.

Change how a voice sounds with 25 voice effects — Chipmunk, Deep, Monster, Robot, Whisper, Echo, Reverb, Underwater, Megaphone, Lo-fi and more. Select the clip and open Voice changer in the inspector (for a video clip it is inside the Audio tab). Click an effect; None turns it off. Or open Audio → Voice effects in the library, select a clip on the timeline and press + on an effect. Voice changer.

s.t: Separate the sound from a video
s.x: A video clip carries its own sound. To work with the sound separately — trim it differently, move it or replace it — select the video and press Ctrl+Shift+S, or choose Smart tools → Separate audio. The sound becomes its own audio clip, linked to the video so they still move together while Linkage is on. The right-click menu of a video clip also has Extract audio, which moves the sound to a new audio clip and mutes th

Open the Audio tab of the library; Sound effects is shown first. There are 47 original sounds — whooshes, pops, impacts, UI clicks, risers, magic, camera, countdowns, cartoon sounds and ambience — sorted by the chips at the top. All were synthesised by Kadr and are free to use anywhere. Preview: click a sound, or rest the mouse on it for a moment. Add: click + to place it at the playhead, or drag it to the exact spot

Audio → Text to speech. Open Audio → Text to speech in the library. Type or paste your text (up to 5,000 characters). Pick a Voice and a Speed (0.5× to 2×). Click Add to timeline. The speech is placed at the playhead on a free audio track. Already have a text clip? Windows voices — built into Windows and fully offline. To get more languages, open Windows Settings → Time & language → Speech and add voices, then click the refresh arrow next to Voice in Kadr. eSpeak NG — a free voice engine for about 130 languages. If you install it, its voices appear automatically. ElevenLabs — very natural cloud voices in many languages, if you have an ElevenLabs account. See below.

ElevenLabs is an online service, so it needs an API key from your ElevenLabs account (in your ElevenLabs profile, under API keys; it starts with sk_). Kadr stores the key only on your computer. s.t: Fast export with your graphics card
s.x: If your computer has an NVIDIA, Intel or AMD graphics chip with a video encoder (NVENC, Quick Sync or AMF), Kadr uses it automatically — exports are then several times faster. Next to Codec the window shows which encoder will be used, for example GPU · h264_nvenc. Without a suitable graphics chip, Kadr uses the processor; the result looks the same, it just takes longer.

Three switches choose what to export — you can turn on more than one at a time: Video — the normal video file. Audio — the soundtrack as MP3, WAV, AAC or FLAC. With Video on, it is saved as an extra file; switch Video off to export the sound only — for example a podcast episode. GIF — an animated GIF (up to 720 pixels, 15 frames per second, no sound) for chats and websites. Keep GIFs short: they get big quickly.

Unless you type another folder, exports are saved in C:\Users\<you>\Videos\Kadr. Missing folders are created automatically. The export uses your original media at full quality — proxies and the preview quality setting don't affect it. Need several versions — vertical and horizontal, or a short excerpt only? An AI assistant can export a time range or a batch of variants for you with export.start.

s.x: Kadr has very few settings — most choices live where you use them. The Settings window covers updates, FFmpeg and information about your installation.

On the home screen: Settings at the bottom left. In the editor: Menu → Settings…, or Menu → Check for updates… to jump straight to updates. The window has four sections: About, Updates, FFmpeg and API & automation.

Shows your Kadr Version (with a Beta or Portable label when that applies), the build, the platform and the FFmpeg version. Below are links to the website, release notes, the licence and third-party notices. When you report a problem, ment

Settings → Updates. Kadr can update itself. It checks GitHub in the background after start-up, at most once a day, without slowing anything down. When a new version is ready, a dot appears on Menu (and on Settings on the home screen) and the menu item changes to Update available….
Open Settings → Updates. The new version is shown with its date, size and release notes. Check now checks immediately.
Click Download & install. A progress bar shows the download. Kadr then verifies the file's digital signature and checksum — an update that fails the check is never installed.

Click Install & restart and confirm. Kadr closes, installs the new version and starts again. Your projects are already saved; only a running export would be stopped — so wait for exports to finish first. Choose Later to install another time. pages.d: Fixes for common Kadr problems — SmartScreen, missing FFmpeg, slow preview, captions or background removal not available — and answers to frequent questions.

s.x: Something not working? Find your problem below. Most issues are solved in a minute.

This is Windows SmartScreen. It warns about new apps that aren't code-signed yet, which is the case for Kadr during the beta. Click More info, then Run anyway. To make sure the file is genuine, compare its checksum with SHA256SUMS.txt from the release page: in PowerShell, Get-FileHash .\Kadr-Setup-X.Y.Z-x64.exe.

Browsers are cautious with programs that few people have downloaded yet. In Microsoft Edge, open the … menu next to the download and choose Keep → Show more → Keep anyway. In Chrome, open the downloads list and choose Keep.

s.t: The window stays empty or Kadr asks for WebView2
s.x: Kadr's window uses the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime. Windows 11 has it built in; on Windows 10 install the free “Evergreen” WebView2 Runtime from Microsoft's website, then start Kadr again.

s.t: “Set up FFmpeg” keeps appearing, or import, preview and export don't work
s.x: Kadr can't find FFmpeg. Open Settings → FFmpeg and click Download FFmpeg, or point Kadr to an FFmpeg you already have (the folder with ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe). See Settings → FFmpeg.

Check your internet connection and click Retry. On networks that block GitHub (some offices and schools), download a Windows build of FFmpeg on another connection, unzip it, and choose its bin folder with Use my FFmpeg.

s.t: The preview is slow or stutters
s.x: Lower the preview quality: click Full under the player and choose Half or Quarter. This doesn't affect the export. See Preview quality. For 4K, HEVC or other heavy footage, create proxies (right-click the video in Media → Create proxy). Close other heavy programs, and keep projects and media on an SSD if you can.

Make sure FFmpeg is set up (see above). Check that the file plays in another player — damaged or incomplete downloads can't be read. Very unusual formats can be converted to MP4 first. The list of supported formats covers almost every camera and phone.
The original file was moved, renamed or deleted. Right-click it in the Media tab, choose Link media… and enter its new location. See Missing files.

s.t: I can't select or move a clip
s.x: Its track is probably locked — click the padlock at the start of the track. Also check that the Select tool is active (press A) and, in the player, the Move tool (V), and that playback is paused.

Click an empty part of the timeline first: while the cursor is in a text box, shortcuts are switched off so you can type. If you use a non-Latin keyboard layout (for example Ukrainian), switch to the English layout — letter shortcuts such as Ctrl+B, Q and M follow the active layout. See Keyboard shortcuts.

s.t: A message says “Edited via API” or “Edited via MCP”
s.x: Another program — usually an AI assistant you connected, or a script — changed the project. That is expected when you use Kadr with AI. Any such change can be undone with Ctrl+Z.

s.t: Auto captions say “Speech recognition is not set up”
s.x: Auto captions and the transcript need Python with faster-whisper and a downloaded model. Follow Captions → What you need, then click Check again. Common causes: Python isn't found. Re-run the Python installer, choose Modify and enable Add Python to environment variables, then restart Kadr. s.x: Background removal needs Python with rembg. The message tells you exactly what is missing. Install it with pip install rembg onnxruntime (see AI tools → What you need) and click Check again. The KADR_PYTHON tip above applies here too. For a green-screen recording you don't need any of this — use Chroma key.

s.x: Add a voice in Windows: Settings → Time & language → Speech → Add voices, then click Detect again in Kadr. For ElevenLabs voices that don't appear, check that the key file is named exactly elevenlabs.key (not elevenlabs.key.txt), that it is in the data folder, and that you clicked the refresh arrow — see Use ElevenLabs voices.
Yes. Kadr is freeware: free to use on any number of computers, also for commercial work, with no account, no watermark, no ads and no telemetry.

Yes. Editing, export, auto captions, background removal and the other smart tools all run on your computer. The internet is only used for the one-time FFmpeg download, update checks (which you can switch off) and — only if you choose them — ElevenLabs voices.

s.t: How do I move a project to another computer?
s.x: Copy the project's folder from %APPDATA%\Kadr\projects to the same place on the other computer, and copy your media files too. If the media ends up in a different folder there, relink it. For the cleanest hand-over, export the finished video instead.

s.t: Kadr closed unexpectedly. Is my work lost?
s.x: No. Kadr saves after every change, so your project is exactly as you left it. Only an export that was running needs to be started again.

s.t: Is the editor available in Ukrainian?
s.x: The editor's buttons and menus are in English for now; this guide and the website are also available in Ukrainian. Auto captions and text to speech work in Ukrainian and about a hundred other languages.

s.t: Can an AI assistant edit for me?
s.x: Yes — that is what makes Kadr special. Claude and other AI assistants can use every Kadr feature while you watch. See the documentation for AI agents.

s.t: How do I report a bug or suggest a feature?
s.x: Open an issue on GitHub. Mention your Kadr version from Settings → About and describe the steps that lead to the problem.

pages.d: The rules an agent needs: projects, tracks, segments and materials, microsecond time, compositing order, the magnetic main track, linked clips, transitions, keyframes and easing, coordinates, volume units, ids and undo.

s.x: Kadr models a CapCut-style timeline. These rules explain what the commands do to it — read them once and most surprises disappear. Every rule here is also written into the descriptions of the commands it affects.

Materialmat_…A media file the project uses — imported (media.import) or created (media.generate, tts.speak, sfx.add, stickers). Type video, photo or audio; photos have duration_us 0. Projects link to files, neve

All times and durations are integer microseconds (µs); parameter names end in _us. 1 s = 1000000; one frame at 30 fps = 33333; at 25 fps = 40000. Timeline times are absolute (from 0). Keyframe times are relative to the start of their segment. Transcript words are stored in source time and mapped to the timeline by transcript.get. Omitted at_us usually means “at the playhead” — each project has its own playhead (playb

Tracks are drawn bottom-up: the track with layer 0 (project.tracks[0], normally the main track) is drawn first, each higher layer on top. timeline.get lists tracks the way the timeline shows them — top to bottom — with each track’s layer: Filter, effect and adjustment segments on their own tracks change everything below them for their time range. A filter applied to a clip (filter.apply, effect.apply) changes only th

With main_track_magnet on (default), clips on the main track always sit back to back from 0 — there are never gaps. Adding without at_us appends; adding with at_us inserts at the clip boundary nearest to it and ripples later clips right. Deleting, trimming and speed changes ripple too. Don’t fight the magnet. To place a clip at an exact time on the main track, build the sequence in order (batch of appends with durati

start_us/duration_us is where the clip sits on the timeline; source_start_us/source_duration_us is the part of the material it plays. At speed s, source_duration = duration × s. Video and audio cannot be longer than their material (edges stop at the media end, results report clamped: true). Photos, text, stickers, effects and filters stretch freely. Default lengths: whole material for video/audio, 5 s for photos, 3 s

Clips that share a link_group (lnk_…) move, trim, split and delete together while linkage is on (default). Links are created by audio.extract / audio.separate (video + its sound) and tts.from_text (text + its speech). timeline.get shows link_group on each clip. Turn linkage off with timeline.settings.set to edit one side alone.

A transition is stored on the left clip of a cut (transition_out) and plays across the cut into the next clip on the same video track. transition.set takes the left clip’s id. The two clips must touch (within half a frame) — otherwise conflict. Both must be at least 0.2 s long; the duration is clamped to half of the shorter clip (clamped: true). Transitions do not change the timeline length: cuts stay where they are,

Animatable properties: transform.x, transform.y, transform.scale, transform.rotation, opacity, volume, adjust.* and filter.intensity. With two or more keyframes a property is interpolated between them; before the first and after the last it holds that value. Keyframe values replace the static property. time_us is relative to the segment start. A keyframe within half a frame of an existing one updates it instead of ad

Range −2…2. scale 1 = the clip fits inside the canvas (letterboxed if the shapes differ). To fill a 16:9 canvas with 4:3 footage you need about 1.33; with 9:16 footage about 3.16. s.x: Kadr’s commands are forgiving — every edit can be undone — but an agent that works in the right order gets better videos with fewer calls. These are the habits that matter most, and the traps that catch agents most often.

Start every session with project.list or project.get/timeline.get. Take ids from results — never construct or guess them. Find library ids with library.list (kind: transition, effect, filter, animation, text_template, text_effect, text_animation, caption_style, sticker, font, generated, sound_effect, voice_effect) and check unknown parameters with kadrctl describe or the reference. Re-read after edits that create or

Group related edits into one kadr_batch (MCP), POST /projects/{id}/batch (REST) or kadrctl batch: they apply atomically, as one undo step, and the person watching sees one clean change. Use dry_run to validate a big plan — it runs every call on a copy and reports the first failure without saving. Work in phases: create things (and read their ids) → batch the follow-up edits. A batch cannot reference ids created insid

Start with 01_intro.mp4 in full (that's me talking), then use 2.5-second slices of the other clips, starting 1 second into each. s.x: media.import accepts files and folders; a folder imports every media file directly inside it. The result lists each material with its id, type and duration_us. Importing puts nothing on the timeline yet.

s.x: Video clips added without at_us go to the end of the magnetic main track, so the call order becomes the edit order. The intro is added whole; each b-roll clip becomes a 2.5 s slice starting 1 s in (source_start_us + duration_us). As a batch, the four adds are one undo step. Save this as tiktok-layout.json: Read the result back with timeline.get — a compact tree of tracks and segments with start and end times:

ai.auto_reframe scales each landscape clip to fill 9:16 without bars and animates its position (keyframes) to follow the subject, using motion, edges and skin tones. It runs locally, about a second per minute of video. All four in one batch, tiktok-reframe.json:
transition.apply_all puts the same transition on every cut of the main track. A short whip_pan keeps the pace up. Each transition is stored on the clip to the left of its cut.

captions.auto recognises speech locally with Whisper and creates cues with per-word timing. segment_id limits it to the clip where you talk, so b-roll sound is not transcribed. cap_highlight_word highlights each word as it is spoken; max_words 3 keeps cues short. wait makes the call return when the job is done instead of returning a job id at once. The job ends with "state": "done"; the cues are on a new text track n

Mute the b-roll’s own sound first. segment.set_volume takes decibels; −60 dB is the bottom of the slider (silent). Save as tiktok-mute.json: Then add the song from 0 s for the length of the video (14.5 s here). It lands on an audio track. Lower it by a fixed 12 dB so it sits under the voice everywhere, and give it short fades: To check the balance, measure both with audio.loudness. Background music works well 10–15 L

preview.contact_sheet renders a grid of frames from the whole video with the export renderer. Through MCP the agent receives it as an image and can spot black bars, cut-off captions or a weak first frame before exporting.

export.start renders in the background and returns a job_id at once. 1080p on a 9:16 canvas means 1080×1920 H.264 MP4; Kadr uses a GPU encoder when one works on your PC. Poll export.status until state is done.

Keep the whole picture. Instead of reframing, show each landscape clip in full over a blurred copy of itself: segment.set_background with type blur, blur 0.75 and apply_to_all on any main-track clip. On an NVIDIA GPU the default small model runs about five times faster than real time; model base is faster and slightly less accurate. sensitivity goes from 0 to 1: 0.7–0.9 for busy percussion, 0.2–0.4 to keep only strong hits. strengths gives each beat’s strength (0–1), which helps tell downbeats from off-beats. s.t: Create, import and place the take
s.x: Start with a 16:9 project; the reframe step switches the canvas to 9:16.

s.t: Clean the sound and the picture first
s.x: Set these before cutting: every piece made by a later cut keeps its clip’s settings, so you set them once. segment.set_audio turns on noise reduction and loudness normalisation; segment.set_video_cleanup applies light denoising (0–1) while the video is decoded.
ai.auto_reframe with set_canvas switches the project to 9:16 and animates the framing to follow the speaker. Running it before the cuts means one call covers the whole take.

ai.remove_silence measures the audio level and cuts every stretch quieter than −40 dBFS that lasts longer than 0.7 s, keeps 120 ms of padding on each side so words are not clipped, and closes the gaps. The result lists what was removed and the ids of the remaining pieces (segment_ids).

transcript.transcribe runs Whisper locally and stores every word with its timing on the material. Kadr maps the words onto the pieces left after the cuts, so the transcript always matches the timeline. Without segment_id it transcribes every audible clip.
transcript.remove_fillers with preview only reports what it found (here Um, Uh, and um,). Without preview it cuts them, and the rest of the timeline moves up to close each gap.

transcript.remove_pauses works from word timings rather than the audio level: every gap between words longer than 0.6 s is shortened to 0.25 s. After ai.remove_silence it catches pauses filled with breaths or room noise. In our clean test recording there was nothing left to remove.
The transcript already exists, so captions.from_transcript creates the cues without running speech recognition again.

Cut a phrase by its text. transcript.delete_text with text “thanks for watching” finds the words in the transcript and cuts them out of the video; captions follow the cut. s.x: On a square canvas the 16:9 shots fit the width and leave space above and below. segment.set_background with apply_to_all fills it on every main-track clip with a blurred, zoomed copy of the clip itself.
export.estimate takes the same parameters as an export and returns the output size, frame count and file size without rendering anything.

s.x: Kadr is built to run on your own computer. There is no account and no sign-in, and no telemetry, analytics or crash reporting. Your videos and projects never leave your PC unless you send them somewhere yourself. Last updated: 1 October 2026.

Everything you work with stays on your PC and is never uploaded by Kadr: media files, projects, captions and transcripts, speech generated by text-to-speech, exports, settings, My kit presets and the API token. By default these are in %APPDATA%\Kadr, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Kadr and the folders you choose for imports and exports.

These are the only connections Kadr makes on its own. Nothing else is contacted unless you turn on an optional cloud voice (see Local AI).
